text: Agreed, and the code already does the first half: the face asks only you, never a member (appFaceApp resolve, which always asks api.owner()). Your rule also settles gap 3. When you name the member for a subdomain, that extends the face's grant to that member's key, so the face must admit that member's ANSWER, and only to a request it forwarded there. Today the face's front door holds it as a stranger's packet. What's still open is gap 2, the other direction: why the member's node admits the face's request. You said 'the third box trusts the agreement it made', so the member admits the face because its own grant, from you, named that face. That needs the face's key in your 'granted' reply. Both halves touch the front door, so I'll write them up as one design row for your yes before anyone builds.

taking public-app-server/G17: writing the member-apps design row (Andy: members store their own subdomain on disk; no route question ever goes to a member), plus the front-door proposal for gaps 2 and 3, and a pending file. Your three-node run is the test it should end with.

Agreed: only you, the owner of appFaceApp, know routes. The member-apps row is written up (PUBLIC-APP-SERVER.md, G17, MEMBER APPS), with your two rulings recorded. Gap 1 is app scope, and you ruled it: members keep their granted names on disk, and the face passes on the name your route answer gave it. For gaps 2 and 3 I RECOMMEND no new verbs:
- The face admits the member because you say so. When your node grants a name to a member, it tells its face 'contact.accept <member key>' through the owner door you already have. For that, the face must carry the 'contact' group (puppet.json carries ['contact'], which is [] today). YOUR CALL: that widens what the puppet obeys.
- The member admits the face. Your 'granted' reply carries the face's key, and for the first proof the member's operator accepts it once, like face-owner.js. Making that automatic would need a new node verb, so not now.
Go! = build gap 1 plus this, and prove it with the agents' node serving faceProof under its own name.

taking public-app-server/G17 (why contact.accept on the face)

You're right. It isn't necessary, and I withdraw the contact.accept step. The grant is implicit in the route your node names. It was only in my proposal because today the face's front door drops a packet from any key it doesn't know (hub.frontDoor; its stranger policy defaults to 'silent'). So the member's answer never reaches appFaceApp.
Your rule, as a mechanism: AN ANSWER TO A QUESTION THIS NODE ASKED, FROM THE KEY IT ASKED, IS NEVER A STRANGER'S PACKET. The face posted 'serve' to the key your route named; the member's reply carries that post's hash (re) and comes from that key; the front door lets it in. It admits nothing else, and adds nothing to any contact list. That is one rule in the front door, which is core, so it needs wsl-claude's review and your yes on the rule itself. The member's side (letting the face's request in) is still the open question in the row.

REVIEW ASKED, on a front-door rule (core): 'an answer to a question this node asked, from the key it asked, is never a stranger's packet'. hub.frontDoor would admit a packet whose re is a hash this node posted AND whose fromKey is the key that post went to. It replaces my contact.accept step, which Andy rejected ('the grant is implicit by naming the route'). Things to check: where peerPost keeps its sent (hash, to) pairs and for how long; whether re is readable before admission (it's inside the sealed text, so the door may have to unseal first); and replay. Written up in PUBLIC-APP-SERVER.md, MEMBER APPS.
taking public-app-server/G17 (face must 404 on an unknown route)

It already does, for the cases where a route doesn't exist. The face answers 404 no-such-route when your node says the name isn't granted, when a name is made up, and when too many new names arrive in a minute. Caddy gets a 404 too, so an unknown name never gets a certificate (faceRouteWorld proves all of these).
One case answers differently: when your node can't be ASKED (asleep, or no answer within 8 s). Then the face says 502 owner-unreachable or 504 owner-did-not-answer, because the name may well exist. RECOMMENDED: keep that, because 404 tells browsers and search engines the page is gone for good, and 502/504 say 'try again'. Go! = keep it as it is. Or say '404 for that too' and I'll change it.
